User: Loris needs three more books to have the same number as Lamont, who has twice the number of books Darryl has. If Darryl has 20 books, calculate the total number of books the three have.
Assistant: <think>

Since Lamont has twice the number of books as Darryl, and Darryl has 20 books, Lamont has 20 * 2 = 40 books. Loris needs three more books to have the same number as Lamont, so Loris has 40 - 3 = 37 books. The total number of books the three have is 20 (Darryl) + 40 (Lamont) + 37 (Loris) = 97 books. </think> <answer> 97 </answer>
